output.headline: ZCG's future dominated October, with proposals to end, shrink or restructure it, alongside NU7 activation prep, bug bounties and a disputed NEAR exit hold.

quiet_but_notable.why: Its title reports a shielded ZEC to EVM atomic swap done with no new signing primitives, technical work that is easy to miss behind the governance debates.
A new version of Zingo-PC, a wallet release thread in the ZingoLabs apps category.
A community project in Community Collaborations introducing a Zcash Grants Hub for browsing ZCG and Coinholder grants and ZecHub DAO proposals.
A Zcash Apps thread on Konclave, titled as a group vault built on FROST.

themes.summary: Four threads argued over ZCG's funding stream: a proposal to end ZCG and send its funds to the NSM, ZCG's own proposal to taper its share, a call from joshs (ZODL) to end the whole Development Fund, and the Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund ZIP offered as a compromise, alongside a Governance thread on switching ZCG elections to Token Holder Voting. Those favouring ending or reducing the stream say coinholders pay through dilution without controlling the spending and that the treasury has grown too large; defenders point to ZCG's record, to the ZIPs that set its allocation, and to weaknesses in coin-weighted voting as the alternative. The threads kept returning to the ZSA poll, whether the same standard should apply to the coinholder-grants stream, and whether the pace is too fast. Whether existing ZCG funds can legally be donated to the NSM was also disputed.
themes.title: The future of ZCG and the Development Fund

themes.summary: A draft ZIP to rename the ZCG stream the Zcash Adoption Pool and aim it at getting ZEC to new users split its thread: supporters cite ZIP 1015's intent and ZECsy's direct onboarding, while critics say contested social causes do not belong in coinholder-funded grants and doubt that direct payments create lasting use. A separate thread, prompted by reactions to the ZECsy booth photos, disagreed about whether those reactions included attacks on identity or were objections to the funding, and about whether the grant funds anything illegal; no agreement was reached. In a less heated thread, regional organisers agreed that the ZCG to ZecHub route for new Ambassadors and emerging communities works, leaving ZecHub's funding and capacity open. A ZECsy community-building grant application was also active in Community Grants.
themes.title: What community and adoption grants should fund

themes.summary: ZCG closed its vulnerability bounty, citing a flood of duplicate and AI-generated reports, and a second thread asked how bounties should work now that such reports are cheap to produce. Participants split between closing the program and keeping it with better filtering; ideas raised included submission bonds, paid triagers, automatic proof-of-concept testing, bounty platforms such as Immunefi (which others said conflict with Zcash's philosophy), severity-limited programs, and discretionary coinholder-vote payouts. Most of the closure thread became reporters asking about delayed payouts, with ZCG describing a staged review and saying eligible bounties would be paid, and ZF acknowledging that one advisory had been left out of its report to ZCG. A grant-update thread for the Zcash Ecosystem Security Lead was also active.
themes.title: Bug bounties after the ZCG program closed

themes.summary: The NU7 thread sets mainnet activation for November 5, 2026 with 25-second blocks and v4 transactions disabled; replies were mostly questions about issuance, confirmations, Sprout funds and ZSAs, independent block-timing counts, and a wallet-readiness list that was partly corrected in-thread. The Crosslink incentivized feature net thread followed sign-ups, releases and two payout rounds, with light debate over whether testnets need prior community support, a disputed Round 1 payout, and whether finality stalls are routine. Both threads gathered evidence from running networks, such as testnet block intervals in one and stall, staking and mining data in the other. Threads titled ZSA Testnet, Sapling withdraw-only discussion kickoff, and recovering an old wallet before the Sprout freeze sit alongside them.
themes.title: Protocol upgrades and testnets

themes.summary: A user reports about $589k USDT held for more than 50 days by NEAR Intents after a Zodl swap, despite a written compliance clearance that was later reversed; the hold is unresolved. Replies debated who is responsible, whether screening funds that leave the shielded pool is normal, whether the rail is custodial, and whether asking for proof of origin undermines the pool's purpose. Suggestions included exit paths with no middleman who can stop a swap and converting smaller amounts per swap. General-category threads titled Zcash + NEAR: Permissionless Cross-Chain Swaps and a shielded ZEC to EVM atomic swap sit alongside it.
themes.title: A held NEAR Intents exit and the routes out of the pool

worth_reading.why: The opening case for ending ZCG and moving its funds to the NSM: coinholders pay through dilution without controlling the spending, and ZCAP includes many grantees. Replies dispute each of these points.

The clearest statement of the defence of ZCG's record: careful, conservative review with only a handful of failures among hundreds of funded proposals, and a grants program's purpose being to back work private investors will not.
Makes the case for the taper as a reasonable compromise to develop into a full proposal; post 9 argues it leaves coinholder representation and accountability unaddressed.

A concession in the payout dispute: ZF says it wrongly left advisory GHSA-pvmv-cwg8-v6c8 out of its report to ZCG and will recommend payout, and it explains how duplicate reports are treated under the program terms.

The clearest statement of the view that the poster could help clear the hold by showing the ZEC's origin or offering viewing keys; post 31 replies that making clearance conditional on that disclosure is a dangerous standard.
A public-evidence list of NU7 readiness across wallets and SDKs, naming those ready upstream and several without NU7 support; posts 31 and 32 corrected parts of it, so read it with them.
